explanation:

q: What was the name of Yudhishtira when Pandavas were in Virata Kingdom to complete Ajnatavasa?
explanation: During the Ajnatavasa at Virata's court Yudhishthira lived as the Brahmin Kanka; Tantripala was Sahadeva's name and Arishtanemi Sahadeva's other alias, so Kanka is the answer.

notes.text: - **Ajnatavasa:** the Pandavas hid in the kingdom of **Virata**; **Yudhishthira** took the name **Kanka** (Bhima – Vallabha, Arjuna – Brihannala).

q: The Chapters of Ramayana are called as one of the following:
explanation: The Ramayana is divided into Kandas (Bala Kanda to Uttara Kanda); Parvas are the books of the Mahabharata and Skandas of the Bhagavata/Puranas.

notes.text: - **Ramayana** chapters = **Kandas** (Mahabharata = **Parvas**).

q: Who translated Mahabharata into Telugu?
explanation: Nannaya, court poet of Rajaraja Narendra, was the first to translate the Mahabharata into Telugu (Adi, Sabha and part of Aranya Parva); Yerrana completed it later, Tulsidas wrote in Awadhi and Mayura in Sanskrit.

notes.text: - **First translator** of the Mahabharata into Telugu = **Nannaya** (APPSC G1 1994; Port Officer 2011; Degree Lecturers 2012; flashcard) – he **started** the Andhra Mahabharatam; Tikkana and Errana completed it.

q: Reading of which Parva in Mahabharat causes rains
explanation: A traditional belief holds that reciting the Virata Parva of the Mahabharata during drought brings rain (Virata Parva parayanam), which is why it is read in temples in dry years.

notes.text: - **Virata Parva:** popular belief that **reading the Virata Parva brings rain** (APPSC Endowment 2022).

notes.text: - **Who translated 15 parvas:** **Tikkana** – not Nannaya, Potana or Errana.

notes.text: - **First translator** of the Mahabharata into Telugu = **Nannaya** (APPSC G1 1994; Port Officer 2011; Degree Lecturers 2012; flashcard) – he **started** the Andhra Mahabharatam; Tikkana and Errana completed it.

The following question contains an

options: Both assertion (A) and reason are true and the reason (R) is the correct explanation of the assertion (A).
Both assertion (A) and reason are true but the reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the assertion
Assertion (A) is true and the reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false and the reason (R) is true.

q: Which among the following statements regarding Tikkana is incorrect?
options: Tikkana was the court poet of the Nellore Telugu Chodas.
Tikkana dedicated Nirvachanottara Ramayana to Manuma Siddhi II.
Marana and Ketana were the disciples of Tikkana.
Andhra Bhasha Bhushanam, the first work on Telugu Grammar, was written by Tikkana.
key_text: Andhra Bhasha Bhushanam, the first work on Telugu Grammar, was written by Tikkana.
explanation: Andhra Bhasha Bhushanam, the first grammar written in Telugu, is Ketana's, not Tikkana's, so statement 4 is incorrect. Tikkana was court poet of the Nellore Chodas, dedicated Nirvachanottara Ramayana to Manumasiddhi II, and taught Marana and Ketana.

notes.text: - **Tikkana statements (FSO):** court poet of the **Nellore Telugu Chodas** ✓; Nirvachanottara Ramayana to **Manumasiddhi II** ✓; **Marana and Ketana** his disciples ✓; **Andhra Bhasha Bhushanam is Ketana's**, not Tikkana's ✗.

q: Who was the first to translate the Ramayana epic into Telugu by 1250 AD?
explanation: Gona Budda Reddy's Ranganatha Ramayanam (by c. 1250) is the first Telugu translation of the Ramayana. Tikkana's Nirvachanottara Ramayana covers only the Uttara Kanda, and Bhaskara's Ramayana came later.

notes.text: - **First Ramayana in Telugu** = **Gona Budda Reddy** (JA NTRUHS; G-W Sachivalayam; APPSC PYQ "by 1250") – not Tikkana, Baddena, Somanatha, Hulakki Bhaskara or Tallapaka Timmakka. "Ranganatha" is the name in the title, not a separate poet.

q: Which of the following is the work of Gona Buddha Reddy?
explanation: Gona Budda Reddy wrote the Ranganatha Ramayanam in dwipada metre. Vichitra Vijayam, Harishchandra Vijayam and Rajasekhara Charitra are other poets' works.

q: Ranganatha Ramayanam was written by?
explanation: Ranganatha Ramayanam was written by Gona Budda Reddy in dwipada metre; Molla wrote the Molla Ramayanam, and Chemakura Venkata Kavi and Rangajamma were 17th-century poets.

q: Which of the following poems is recognized as the greatest dwipada kavyam in Telugu literature?
explanation: Gona Budda Reddy's Ranganatha Ramayana is regarded as the greatest (and first) dwipada kavya in Telugu; Nirvachanottara Ramayana is in padyas and Bhaskara Ramayana is a champu.

q: Which language is popularly known as the 'Italian of the East'?
explanation: Telugu, whose words end in vowels, was called the 'Italian of the East' by the 15th-century Venetian traveller Niccolo de' Conti.

notes.text: - **City described:** **Orugallu (Warangal)** in great detail – markets, temples, nightlife, festivals (APPSC G1 2002 ×2; G2 2002; APPSC PYQ ×2) – not Rajasekhara Charitra, Kalapurnodayam, Nilambari; not Amaravati, Rajamahendravaram or Pithapuram.

q: Official languages of Andhra Pradesh state?
explanation: Telugu is the official language of Andhra Pradesh (since 1966) and Urdu is the second official language (all districts since the 2022 amendment); Hindi is not an official language of the state.

notes.text: - **Character Machaladevi:** a famous courtesan (dancer) of Warangal in **Kreedabhiramam** – not Himabindu, Veyipadagalu or Amuktamalyada.

exam: APPSC Asst. BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains Paper-II 2017
q: The earliest Telugu inscription seen at Vipparla was issued by
explanation: The Vipparla inscription was issued by the Eastern Chalukya Jayasimha Vallabha I; Vishnuvardhana I (Kubja) issued the Chejarla record, not Vipparla.

q: Which is the first inscription in Telugu?
explanation: The Kalamalla inscription (Kadapa, c. 575 CE) of the Renati Chola Erikal Mutturaju Dhananjaya is regarded as the first Telugu inscription; Chejarla and Addanki are later Eastern Chalukya-period records.

q: In which language are the Kakatiya inscriptions given?
explanation:
Most books and keys: Telugu. NextGen (Kakatiyas p.71) calls Sanskrit the Kakatiya royal language with most inscriptions in Sanskrit; the corpus is largely Telugu or bilingual.
Most Kakatiya-period inscriptions are in Telugu, which became the administrative language under them (many are bilingual Sanskrit-Telugu); Prakrit and Pali belong to the earlier Buddhist age.

q: What was the official language of the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi?
explanation:
Most books and keys: Telugu (NextGen previous papers, Rocket #11). Strictly: the grants' prasasti and much of the court record stayed in Sanskrit (NextGen Powerplay #1 Part 5.1 p.9; old app notes said Sanskrit).
APPSC keys and NextGen give Telugu as the official language of the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi: Telugu entered royal records and literature under them (grant details in Telugu, Nannaya at court). Sanskrit stayed the language of the prasasti.

q: Who was the exponent to state that the origin of Telugu is from Sanskrit?
explanation: Chilukuri Narayana Rao (Andhra Bhasha Charitramu) argued that Telugu was born of Sanskrit and the Prakrits; Bishop Caldwell held the opposite, that Telugu is a Dravidian language. (Moved: Telugu language and literature row.)

q: 'Kreedabhiramam' is a?
explanation:
Key: Poetry. Strictly it is a vidhi natakam (street play) in verse, not a poem (NextGen Kakatiyas p.3).
Kreedabhiramam is a Telugu vidhi natakam (street play) written in verse, so among the options it is poetry. 'Kreeda' means amusement, not sport, and it is no grammar.

notes.text: - **Mitakshara into Telugu:** **Ketana** (G1 2010 re-exam; G1 PYQ; APPSC PYQ) – not Vijnaneswara himself, Visweswara, Madiki Singana, Shivadevayya, Sayana or Baddena.

q: Which of the following cities is described as the city of actors in Kreedabhiramam?
explanation: Kreedabhiramam describes Orugallu (Warangal) as the abode of actors and drama artists, with its markets, temples and nightlife. Dwarasamudram, Devagiri and Madhura were Hoysala, Yadava and Pandya capitals.

notes.text: - **Other Kakatiya law/ethics works:** Purushartha Saramu – **Shivadevayya**; Sakala Niti Sammatamu – **Madiki Singana**; Nitisastra Muktavali and Sumati Satakam – Baddena.

q: Prataparudra - Yashobhushana was written by
explanation: Prataparudra Yasobhushanam (Prataparudriyam) is a Sanskrit alankara work by Vidyanatha, court poet of Prataparudra II; it is not by Ketana, Baddena or Tikkana.
